sentences.text:
On The 6 th Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 3154 of 2009

The Manager United India Insurnace Co.
 Versus
 Poonamchand & Ors.

And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Pradeep Gupta - Advocate for the appellant.

Order 
This misc. appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is against award passed in MACC No.30/2009 dated 23.09.2009 whereby the injured/applicant has been awarded an amount of Rs.2,90,000/- with interest @ 6 p.a from the date of application.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance company submits that in this case FIR was belatedly lodged looking to the fact that incident occurred on 10.09.2005 and FIR was lodged on 12.09.2005.

The belated FIR reveals that it is a case of false involvement of the vehicle and hence, prays for setting aside the impugned award wherein liability has been fastened on the Insurance company for the payment of award amount.
3. None for the respondents.
4. Heard and considered the submission and perused the record.
5.
It is well settled that mere delayed FIR is not a ground to believe that it is case of false involvement of the vehicle.

From the perusal of record NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8906 2 MA-3154-2009 available it is apparent that the learned Claims Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence available on record and came to the conclusion that the accident took place by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Auto-Rikshaw CPM-1341.

Thus, even on reappraisal of the evidence available on record it is not found that learned Claims Tribunal has committed any error in fastening the liability of payment of compensation upon the appellant/Insurance company.
Ex-consequentia, the appeal which is devoid of any substance, fails and is hereby dismissed maintaining the award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
